steps.what: Examine food type, color and bouquet and measure moisture where required
Grade food products against applicable regulations and product criteria

tasks.design: Keep current grading criteria in {DOCS} and record the worker's grade in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Retain sensory examination and interpretation; a numeric moisture threshold alone does not replace grading by bouquet, colour and product condition.
tasks.previous_blocker: Grading combines measurements with sensory judgement and product-specific standards.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing measurement and record tools help, but the digest establishes no automated grading capability for this task.
tasks.still_hard: Borderline samples, representative sampling and defects outside the measured property.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising an unusual sample and knowing when quality review is needed.
tasks.altitude: Grading responsibility and time stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: The food-processing digest does not establish automated sensory grading; no physical examination or grading saving is proposed.

assumptions: Boundary is sample examination and grade assignment, not production control or product development. Separate quality-team work is outside this denominator and unchanged.
Worker produces sample observations and any moisture result in s1 with all60 hours retained. No machine depends on assumed structured colour, bouquet or pass/fail labels.
Native criteria and measurement records come first. Zero incremental upkeep because no new grading system or process is introduced.
unknowns: Product-specific grade criteria and measurement methods
Role's authority to assign official grades
research_questions: Which grading properties require sensory judgement even when moisture is measured?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives net0 after zero upkeep. Sensory examination60 and grading40 remain fully counted; no existing instrument runtime is saved labour.

steps.what: Define recipe objectives, ingredient limits and process constraints
Formulate candidate recipes or modifications and check quantities and ingredient constraints

loop.purpose: Suggest bounded recipe variations within the worker's brief
loop.input: Existing formula, permitted ingredients, target properties and process limits
loop.output: Candidate ingredient quantities and proposed changes with stated rationale
loop.check: Worker checks feasibility and each substitution; deterministic arithmetic checks totals and cost from checked specifications, never inferred allergens
loop.stop: Unknown ingredient, unsupported safety claim or impossible process sends formulation to manual work; no candidate goes directly to production
loop.why_not_simpler: Native formula scaling is tried first; proposing a changed formulation can need bounded hypothesis generation

steps.what: Check trial safety and test the candidate recipe through preparation and sensory evaluation
Choose the final recipe modification and record the exact validated version

tasks.design: Use native formula scaling and ingredient records in {OPS_SYSTEM} first. A bounded model may suggest variants for human review, but deterministic calculations use checked specifications and physical trials establish recipe performance before the worker records a final version in {DOCS} or {OPS_SYSTEM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exploring variations can require repeated drafting and recalculation before a trial.
tasks.enabler_now: Formula systems and recipe-variant drafting capabilities exist, without proving food batchmaker labour savings.
tasks.still_hard: Taste, texture, stability, process feasibility and safe scale-up cannot be inferred from a plausible formula.
tasks.human_edge: Judging trial results and rejecting a technically plausible recipe that does not work.
tasks.altitude: Potentially less candidate drafting; physical trial and recipe responsibility stay unchanged.

reach.learn: Which changes require shelf-life or safety testing beyond a bench trial

evidence.claim: nextfood.ai drafts formulations according to the digest; synthetic screening does not establish physical recipe performance.
Aptean Bakery ERP keeps formulas, allergen flags and product cost; ingredient truth still depends on maintained specifications.
The60% remaining candidate-drafting time and5-hour upkeep are provisional task scenarios, not measured batchmaker results.

assumptions: Boundary is a bounded recipe modification from brief through trial and recorded version, not a full commercial launch or shelf-life validation. Food-technologist and quality approvals required for release remain separate unchanged work; this file grants no production-release authority.

Worker s1 produces product target, batch basis, allowed ingredients, ingredient IDs, specification versions and process limits within its full20 hours. Suppliers produce ingredient composition and allergen declarations in their existing specification process; worker checks missing or changed specifications in s1. No calculation runs on model-invented allergen or safety data; missing inputs cause manual formulation.
